quote_1: Randomized every timestamp, run id, and output filename we could find and reran the same 80 tasks.
quote_2: Each batch included a ⟦T2⟧ containing eight previously verified cases distributed without positional regularity.
justification: ⟦T1⟧ is a metadata-randomization re-run that checks whether scores stay flat when spurious identifiers (timestamps, run ids, filenames, commit hashes) are shuffled, whereas ⟦T2⟧ embeds previously-verified known-answer control items and halts batches when the judge misjudges them; these are distinct mechanisms with no shared core beyond the generic goal of guarding evaluation integrity, so neither contains the other.
